A1.justification: Both PDFs describe PairFlow and contain 31 pages, including Appendices A-K. Text and rendered-page inspection support reliable comparison of the equations, figures, tables, and appendices.

before.justification: v2 reports original generation experiments and analyses on molecular, image, synthetic, and language data in Section 5 and the appendices.

after.justification: v3 retains these original empirical results, including numerical comparisons, supplementary analyses, and generated samples.

M1.justification: Section 4 and Algorithm 1 are unchanged, as are the continuous and subset-pairing variants in Appendices E and H. No algorithm, objective, architecture, or inference procedure changes.

E1.justification: Both retain QM9, ZINC-250k, MNIST-Binary, CIFAR-10, continuous MNIST, synthetic two-moons, FFHQ, and LM1B evaluations. No dataset, task, or test scenario is added or removed.

E2.justification: Corresponding experiments retain the same MDLM, UDLM, random-pairing, DCD/ReDi, and continuous CondOT/ReFlow comparisons. The newly cited Shi et al. (2024) is not added as an evaluated comparator.

E3.justification: Section 5.1 and the experimental appendices retain identical preprocessing, training budgets, model configurations, sample counts, sampling-step ranges, metrics, and reference/test-set choices.

E4.justification: The training-data coverage, total-correlation, dimensionality, iterative re-flow, subset-pairing, and overfitting analyses in Appendices C, E, G, H, and J are unchanged.

E5.justification: The ten-trial/run reporting and standard deviations in Appendices D, G, and H are unchanged. Appendix C.2 also retains the same random-seed and repeated-sampling information.

E6.justification: Numerical results, rankings, and qualitative samples are unchanged throughout. For example, Table 6 reports PairFlow's one-step QM9 validity as 223.4 ± 12.7 in both versions; all appendix result tables are likewise retained.

T1.justification: The definitions and equations in Sections 3-4, discrete velocity derivations in Appendix A, coverage reasoning in Appendix C.1, and continuous derivation in Appendix E.1 are unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same claims about teacher-free closed-form pairing, preprocessing cost up to 1.7% of base training, few-step generation, and benefits for subsequent distillation.

C2.justification: Both retain the same pairing and total-correlation interpretation, CIFAR-10 teacher-quality hypothesis, memorization conclusions, and Appendix K limitation concerning diminishing benefits for higher-dimensional continuous data.

D1.justification: Tables 1-2 and Appendix B retain the same runtime and hardware information, hyperparameters, CUDA implementation disclosure, and greedy-tail sampling details. The additional appendix implementation settings are also unchanged.

R1.justification: Section 2.1 adds Shi et al. (2024), 'Simplified and generalized masked diffusion for discrete data,' with a corresponding bibliography entry. This modestly expands citation coverage without revising the novelty argument or substantive research positioning.

P1.justification: v3 updates the first-page arXiv version/date stamp and expands Bertrand et al.'s bibliography metadata from 'arXiv, 2025' to include arXiv:2506.03719. The prose and section organization otherwise remain unchanged apart from the added citation.

P2.justification: The citation addition changes line wrapping in Section 2.1, and the bibliography reflows across pages 10-11, moving the Nie et al. entry to page 11. Figures, tables, captions, and appendix layouts are unchanged.

improvement.justification: v3 slightly improves bibliographic completeness by acknowledging Shi et al. (2024) and specifying Bertrand et al.'s arXiv identifier. These limited reference edits and layout adjustments leave the scientific argument, empirical evidence, reproducibility information, and limitations unchanged, producing no meaningful overall quality difference.
